name: Pale Expanse

stars.name: Pale Expanse A
stars.notes: Bright yellow-white anchor of the system, burning hot enough to bleach every world that faces it.

stars.name: Pale Expanse B
stars.notes: Dim red companion swinging through a wide 480 AU orbit, trailing its own small retinue of frozen rocks.

planets.name: First Scorch
planets.notes: Half-molten cinder skimming the F-star; lander hulls recorded here have all failed inspection.

planets.name: Ledger
planets.notes: Survey beacons mark platinum-group veins running like ledger lines through its crust.

planets.name: Whitesand
planets.notes: Bleached dune world used for consortium equipment endurance trials; nothing survives a full season.

planets.name: Brinehall
planets.notes: Ammonia-chilled seas with no native life; biotech firms lease sampling rights they never exercise.

planets.name: Grand Pallid
planets.notes: Washed-out giant skimmed by tanker runs; nineteen moons serve as navigational mileposts for the haul lanes.

planets.name: Hoarfrost
planets.notes: Glacial world hosting Coldmoor Depot's fuel cracking plants on its tidally warmed underside.

planets.name: Dimwether
planets.notes: Grey, cratered, and utterly unremarkable, which is exactly why someone buried a cache vault there, unregistered.

planets.name: Farthing Ice
planets.notes: Last body claimed before the survey line was drawn; worth exactly what its name implies.

planets.name: Ember Row
planets.notes: S-type captive of Pale Expanse B, glowing dull red under its master's close light.

planets.name: Redfoot
planets.notes: Comet-like capture trailing vapor whenever B warms; a favored smuggler waypoint off all charts.

anomalies.name: The Pale Bloom
anomalies.notes: Ore sampled near the bloom shifts isotope ratios between extraction and refinery; assays never match twice, wrecking futures contracts.

asteroid_belts.name: Ledgerline Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Consortium strip-mines run around the clock; the Pale Bloom sits somewhere in its middle reaches and everyone pretends otherwise.

asteroid_belts.name: Frostmarch Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Volatiles harvested for Hoarfrost's cracking plants; quiet, cold, and patrolled by nothing but boredom.

stations.name: Assay Zero
stations.notes: Company town carved into a nickel-iron host rock; rotation shifts run on bonus schedules.

stations.name: Coldmoor Depot
stations.notes: Fuel and transponder services for tanker crews; the closest thing the Expanse has to civilization.

faction_control.notes: Held under corporate charter; company law applies dockside and throughout the belts, enforced by contracted wardens.

history: Consortium surveyors staked the Expanse during the platinum rush and wrote the charter that made company law its only law.
Assay Zero struck the Ledgerline's mother lode in a single season, anchoring a permanent haul route through the Sallow Stretch.
Refinery assays began failing to match belt samples after the Pale Bloom appeared, prompting an internal audit that has yet to conclude.
description: The Pale Expanse is a washed-out watercolor of a system: a hot yellow-white sun, ten bleached worlds, and a distant red dwarf dragging two frozen captives through the outer dark. Nothing here is lush or kind. Everything is ore, ice, and glare, arranged across wide orbits built for long hauls and longer shifts.

It thrives anyway, because the Ledgerline Belt is one of the richest metallic strikes in the Stretch. Assay Zero's six hundred miners feed tanker convoys that give the system its steady moderate traffic, while Coldmoor Depot sells them fuel and takes their scrip. The Greymarket Consortium's charter is the only government anyone acknowledges, and its wardens keep the peace with timesheets and tasers.

The Pale Bloom is the secret everyone works around. Somewhere in the belt's middle reaches, matter itself misbehaves, and every assay that passes near it comes back different. The consortium's audit has dragged on for years, quietly buying back contaminated contracts. Miners whisper that the Bloom is spreading toward the shipping lanes, and that Dimwether's unregistered cache vault holds whatever the first survey team found and chose not to report.
